high.title: Dollar Jumps to R$ 5.06 and Accumulates Gains of More Than 3% with 'Flávio Risk' and Middle East in Focus
high.summary: The USD/BRL exchange rate surged to R$ 5.0678 on Friday, marking a 1.63% daily gain amid increased risk aversion driven by geopolitical tensions and domestic electoral risk pricing. The dollar reached an intraday high of R$ 5.0818 (+1.92%), the highest level in nearly a month. For the week, USD/BRL accumulated a significant 3.55% appreciation against the real. The move followed broader dollar strength globally, with the DXY index gaining 0.47% to 99.292 points. Domestic political risks are back in focus as markets digest electoral uncertainties, particularly around Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy and his connections to Banco Master's owner Daniel Vor. This political risk premium is overshadowing the typically BRL-positive impact of rising oil prices, given Brazil's commodity exporter status. FX traders should monitor political developments closely as electoral uncertainty could drive further volatility in the real, potentially testing the R$ 5.10 resistance level if risk-off sentiment persists.

medium.title: Ibovespa Below 180,000 Points: Is There Still Room for Gains in the Stock Market?
medium.summary: The Ibovespa has retreated from its April highs near 200,000 points, falling 4% in the first seven trading sessions of May and dropping below 180,000 points on Tuesday for the first time since March. Despite accumulating 16% gains year-to-date through April, analysts cite a more challenging macroeconomic environment reducing risk appetite for Brazilian equities. Global inflation expectations and potential impacts from US monetary policy are key concerns affecting the local market's performance outlook.

medium.title: Real Estate Investment Funds Gained Strength with Mercado Livre, Amazon, Shein and Shopee; See 3 REITs That Can Take Advantage of the Scenario
medium.summary: The IFIX real estate fund index gained 1.53% in April, outperforming the Ibovespa, driven primarily by logistics REITs benefiting from e-commerce expansion. Major tenants including Mercado Livre, Amazon, Shein, and Shopee are driving demand for warehouse space across Brazil. With e-commerce revenue surpassing R$ 235 billion in 2025 and expected 33% growth through 2028, logistics real estate remains a beneficiary of structural digital commerce trends.
